hypotheses.persona: Remote worker with structured morning routine
hypotheses.rationale: Consistent early desk/table usage (07:00-08:00) across all days, including weekends, strongly suggests a professional or serious academic routine. The addition of dinner/bowl events confirms a standard daily cycle without major disruption.

Remains unlikely due to the rigid consistency of the morning block. However, the lack of explicit 'work' objects (laptop) on weekends keeps this slightly viable if they study casually or use digital-only resources.
Contradicted by consistent early morning activity (07:00+) and late night sleep (21:45). Probability remains negligible.

Day 5, 07:10 — coffee_mug at table_d1 (confirms morning ritual persists on Saturday, sharpening 'structured routine' hypothesis)
Day 6, 07:40 — coffee_mug at desk_o1 (CRITICAL: Desk used on Sunday morning, contradicting 'work only M-F' assumption; suggests weekend work/reading routine)
Day 6, 09:12 — reading_glasses at desk_o1 (Confirms sustained presence at desk on Sunday morning, likely reading or light work)
Day 7, 07:00 — coffee_mug at table_d1 (Reinforces consistent early morning start on Monday, confirming the routine is not weekend-specific)
Day 7, 18:04 — plate at table_d1 (Indicates evening meal preparation/consumption, establishing a standard dinner time around 18:00-19:00)
Day 8, 07:47 — coffee_mug at desk_o1 (Reinforces consistent early morning start on Tuesday, confirming the routine is not weekend-specific)
Day 8, 11:45 — fork at table_d1 (Indicates midday meal/snack, suggesting a break in the morning routine or a second meal)
Day 8, 13:45 — reading_glasses at coffee_table_l1 (Suggests afternoon leisure/reading activity, distinct from morning desk work)
Day 9, 14:17 — remote at sofa_l1 (Confirms afternoon leisure block, consistent with post-lunch relaxation pattern)
notes: Routine remains highly stable. Day 9 adds no new discriminators for persona but confirms the afternoon leisure block (remote at 14:17). The 11:07 sink event is mundane cleanup. The 16:17 remote move is likely minor repositioning. Key open question: When does the laptop appear? The 'work' label is inferred from duration and headset, not direct observation of work hardware. Afternoon pattern: 13:45 glasses (reading) -> 14:17 remote (TV/leisure). Evening pattern: 18:00 dinner -> 21:45 sleep prep.
